title: The scheme-theoretic centre of a reductive group is of multiplicative type
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. A torus is a group scheme becoming $(\mathbf G_m)^d$ over $\bar k$ for some integer $d\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m$ is as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. A group scheme is of multiplicative type if over $\bar k$ it is isomorphic to a closed subgroup scheme of $(\mathbf G_m)^n$ for some $n\geq0$. A smooth affine group is unipotent if in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation all its geometric points are unipotent matrices, meaning $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. The centre $Z(G)$ denotes the subgroup functor whose $A$-points commute with every element of $G(A')$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$. Let $G$ be smooth, geometrically connected and reductive, where reductive means that $G_{\bar k}$ has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup scheme. Then $Z(G)$ is of multiplicative type. No smoothness or connectedness of $Z(G)$ is asserted.

source.place: Corollary 17.62(a), printed p.372; its proof uses a geometric maximal torus and Proposition 17.61(a), printed p.372, with existence over the base from Corollary 17.83, printed p.379.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change], the centre functor in the statement is represented by a closed subgroup scheme $Z(G)\subseteq G$, and with $K=\bar k$ its base change satisfies $Z(G)_{\bar k}=Z(G_{\bar k})$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G_{\bar k}$, where $Z(G_{\bar k})$ is the centre functor of $G_{\bar k}$ on commutative $\bar k$-algebras. Since multiplicative type is defined by a condition over $\bar k$, it suffices to show that $Z(G_{\bar k})$ is isomorphic to a closed subgroup scheme of some $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ over $\bar k$.

source.place: Proposition 1.92 and the following paragraph, printed pp.33--34 (formation of the centre commutes with field extension, as used in the proof of Corollary 17.62(c), p.373).

proof.text: Put $H=G_{\bar k}$. It is affine of finite type over $\bar k$ ($\bar k[H]=k[G]\otimes_k\bar k$ is finitely generated), smooth (local finite presentation and the lifting property of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] pass to $H$ by composing a given $T\to H$ with $H\to G$, lifting over $k$, and pairing the lift with $T'\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$), connected because $G$ is geometrically connected, and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup scheme, which is the reductivity hypothesis on $G$. Thus $H$ is reductive in the sense of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] over the algebraically closed field $F=\bar k$, which supplies a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$, $T\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^r$ over $\bar k$. Only this existence clause is used, not the Borel subgroup.

source.place: Choice of a maximal torus in the proof of Corollary 17.62(a), printed p.372; existence over an algebraically closed field as in Theorem 17.9, pp.353--355.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] over the field $\bar k$, which is its own algebraic closure, to the smooth geometrically connected reductive group $H$ and the torus $T$; its hypothesis that $T$ becomes maximal over the algebraic closure is the maximality of $T$ in $H$ from Step 2. It gives $C_H(T)=T$ as subgroup functors. For every commutative $\bar k$-algebra $A$, every $z\in Z(H)(A)$ commutes with every element of $H(A')$, hence of $T(A')$, for every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$; so $Z(H)(A)\subseteq C_H(T)(A)=T(A)$ for all $A$, including nonreduced $A$. Taking $A=\bar k[Z(H)]$ and the universal point, the surjection $\bar k[H]\to\bar k[Z(H)]$ factors through $\bar k[H]\to\bar k[T]$, so $\bar k[T]\to\bar k[Z(H)]$ is surjective and $Z(H)$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $T\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^r$. By Step 1, $Z(G)_{\bar k}=Z(H)$, which is the definition of multiplicative type. No smoothness or connectedness of $Z(G)$ is used or asserted.

source.place: Proposition 17.61(a) and the proof of Corollary 17.62(a), printed p.372.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 17.62(a), p.372, using Proposition 17.61(a) over the algebraic closure and Proposition 1.92 for base change of the centre.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-88b0b1dcf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX for C5 (an unneeded generalisation of an existing node). The item's statement is correct, unchanged and matches Milne Cor. 17.62(a), p.372: G smooth, geometrically connected and reductive, with the all-test-algebras centre, and multiplicative type defined over k-bar. Checked on GL_n, SL_p in characteristic p (centre mu_p, non-reduced), PGL_2, a non-split torus and G=1. The delivered proof is correct. However, the new node lem-sfb-geometrically-maximal-torus-exists (Milne 17.83, a k-rational torus that becomes maximal over k-bar; this is Grothendieck's theorem via 17.82/17.81, with the finite-field case via 17.99) is not needed. Multiplicative type is a condition over k-bar, lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change already gives Z(G)_{k-bar}=Z(G_{k-bar}), and the existing lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure (same unit) gives a split maximal torus of a reductive group over an algebraically closed field. The report's duplicate search missed borel-pair-structure. The rewritten item has three steps. Step 1: representability and base change of the centre. Step 2: G_{k-bar} is affine of finite type, smooth (shown from def-sbc-smooth-morphisms), connected and reductive, so borel-pair-structure gives T, isomorphic to G_m^r. Step 3: lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer over k-bar gives C(T)=T, so Z(G_{k-bar}) lies in T for all algebras, the universal point gives a closed immersion, and the conclusion is multiplicative type. proof_deps, source places and the split_report summary are updated. No cycle. The kept new node, reductive-torus-self-centralizer, is exactly Milne Prop. 17.61(a), p.372, with the 1.92 centralizer. It is statement only and self-contained, it was tested on SL_2 including characteristic 2, and both hypotheses are needed (T=1 and G_a x G_m are counterexamples without them). No duplicate exists.
